title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Express Criminal Law Provisions before and after Amendment in Judicial Documents

articles.content_en:
1. Depending on the circumstances of the case, when a judgment document cites the provisions of the Criminal Law revised by the Fifth Session of the Eighth National People's Congress on March 14, 1997, the citation shall be expressed according to the specific circumstances as follows:
(1) Where the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law have not been amended after the revised Criminal Law came into force, or have been amended but the current effective provisions are cited, the citation shall be expressed as "Article XX of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China".
(2) Where the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law have been amended, and the provisions before the amendment are cited, the citation shall be expressed as "Article XX of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China as revised in 1997".
(3) Where the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law have been amended more than once, and the provisions before the last amendment are cited, the citation shall be expressed as "Article XX of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China as amended by the Amendment (X) to the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China of XXXX year".

2. Depending on the circumstances of the case, when a judgment document cites the provisions of the Criminal Law before the revision by the Fifth Session of the Eighth National People's Congress on March 14, 1997, the citation shall be expressed as "Article XX of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China of 1979".

3. Depending on the circumstances of the case, when a judgment document cites the provisions of a separate criminal law, the specific provisions of the corresponding regulation, supplementary provision, or decision shall be directly cited.

4. The Notice of the Supreme People's Court on How to Cite the Names of the Criminal Law Before and After the Revision in Judgments (Fa [1997] No. 192) and the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Cite the Criminal Law Amendments in Judgments (Fa Shi [2007] No. 7) shall no longer apply.
